name: Ligurian
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Ligurian (ligu1248) is not in the catalog. All six Glottolog title hits are keyword artefacts: Dresher & van der Hulst 1998, Mellander 2005 and Noel Aziz Hanna 2013 are general prosodic-theory papers with no Ligurian content (abstracts/snippets checked; Ghini 2001 cites D&vdH only for mora theory); Hyman 2019 is Bantu and Kraehenmann 2003 is Alemannic. The one relevant item is Ghini 2003 on the Miogliola dialect (paywalled De Gruyter; snippets recovered give p. 424 ex. (4): moraic trochee, right-to-left, End Rule Right, final light rhymes extrametrical, final consonants catalectic; light-penult stress lexically marked). Best first-hand statement read: Toso 1997 Grammatica del genovese §16-17 (snippet, re-fetched sources this sweep): stress on final, penult or antepenult, fourth-from-last only with enclitics, secondary stress two syllables before the primary — i.e. lexical stress within a three-syllable window, matching Ghini (Miogliola) and Azaretti 1977 (Ventimigliese). Nothing full-text and open was found for a modern source; open 19th-c. texts on file (Randaccio 1894: Genoese keeps the Latin accent position; Casaccia 1876 on accent marks) are consistent but weaker. fetched sources records (sweep_fetches/, google_books_snippets/feed4-6_*.xml) and. Priority acquisitions: Ghini 2003/2001 full text (medium) and Toso 1997 print (for page numbers); none of the other five items is worth acquiring for this language.

new_statements.quote: Posizione dell'accento 16. L'accento può cadere sull'ultima (mangiâ [manga] 'mangiare'), sulla penultima (bagno [báñu] 'bagno') o sulla terzultima sillaba (càrega [káreġa] 'carica'), ed anche sulla quartultima in caso di combinazioni di forme verbali e pronomi enclitici (pòrtighelo [pòrtigelu] 'portacelo'). 17. Accanto all'accento principale, esiste un accento secondario che, in genere, cade due sillabe prima del principale (paccialan [páčalán] 'bonaccione') o su una vocale lunga atona (cösetta [kóséta] 'cosuccia').
new_statements.translation: Position of the accent. 16. The accent may fall on the last syllable (mangiâ 'to eat'), on the penultimate (bagno 'bath') or on the antepenultimate syllable (càrega 'load'), and also on the fourth-from-last in combinations of verb forms and enclitic pronouns (pòrtighelo 'bring it to him'). 17. Beside the main accent there is a secondary accent which generally falls two syllables before the main one (paccialan 'good-natured fellow') or on a long unstressed vowel (cösetta 'little thing'). [Snippet scanned: '[manga]' has lost its diacritic, presumably [manğá].]
new_statements.citation: Toso, Fiorenzo (1997). Grammatica del genovese: varietà urbana e di koinè. Recco: Le Mani. x+295 pp.
new_statements.locator: Ch. I (Fonologia), 'Posizione dell'accento', §§16-17; page not visible in the snippets (the adjacent orthographic-accent snippet carries the running footer '29 Grammatica del genovese')
new_statements.rule_in_words: Genoese word stress is not fixed: it falls on the final, penultimate or antepenultimate syllable depending on the word (a three-syllable window from the right), extended to the 4th-6th syllable from the end only in verb + enclitic-pronoun clusters. Toso's orthographic rules (written accent obligatory on antepenult-and-earlier stress and on oxytones, with listed exceptions) imply that penultimate stress is the unmarked/default position, but the snippets show no explicit statement of a default.
new_statements.secondary_stress: §17: a secondary stress generally falls two syllables before the main stress (paccialan [páčalán]) or on a long unstressed vowel (cösetta [kóséta]).
new_statements.exceptions: Stress beyond the antepenult (quartultima, quintultima, sestultima) only in verb-form + enclitic pronoun combinations (pòrtighelo, asbrìvighelo, méttimeghelo); orthographic accent rules exempt æ/eu and treat -n-final and -ìa/-ùa words separately.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms), urban Genoese and the Ligurian koiné; enclitic clusters treated as single prosodic words. Ghini 2001 (Miogliola dialect) gives a metrical account: moraic trochee assigned right-to-left with right-edge catalexis, stress on light penults lexically marked.
new_statements.identity_note: Toso 1997 describes urban Genoese and the Genoese-based Ligurian koiné, the reference variety for ligu1248 (Glottolog dialect code for Genoese not verified here). Ghini 2001/2003 describe Miogliola, the Ligurian dialect of Mioglia (Savona) at the Ligurian-Piedmontese border, not Genoese.

new_statements.translation: Stress may fall on the last syllable (mangiâ 'to eat'), on the penult (bagno 'bath') or on the antepenult (càrega 'load'), and even on the fourth-from-last in combinations of verb forms with enclitic pronouns (pòrtighelo 'bring it to us'). 17. new_statements.citation: Toso, Fiorenzo (1997). Grammatica del genovese: varietà urbana e di koinè. Recco: Le Mani. Cap. I (Fonologia), §16 'Posizione dell'accento' (and §17 on secondary stress).
new_statements.locator: Cap. I Fonologia, §16 'Posizione dell'accento' (Google Books snippet view, id akJGsjires4C; page number not shown by the feed, the orthographic-accent rule two sections later carries footer p. 29)
new_statements.reading: Genoese Ligurian has lexical (non-predictable) stress confined to the last three syllables: oxytone, paroxytone or proparoxytone, with pre-antepenultimate stress only in verb+enclitic clusters; a rhythmic secondary stress two syllables before the primary. This is the reference grammar of the standard variety and is consistent with Ghini's formal Miogliola account (right-edge weight-sensitive trochee with lexically marked light-penult stress; final stress in papá, virtú) and with Azaretti 1977 for Ventimigliese (paroxytone, proparoxytone, and also oxytone, plus enclitic clusters). Access is snippet-only (Google Books); the passage was read verbatim but not on a full page.

sources.citation: Randaccio, Carlo (1894). Dell'idioma e della letteratura genovese; studio seguito da un Vocabolario etimologico genovese. Roma: Forzani.
sources.note: Historical remarks only: Genoese, like all Romance, rests 'sulla persistenza dell'accento tonico. Là dov'era l'accento latino, ivi trovansi gli accenti italiano, francese, genovese' (scanned line 4072); nearly all verbs end in strongly stressed -a/-i, endings -ou/-iu stressed on the penultimate vowel (p. 34ff). No synchronic rule.
